| [TERM-090](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-090.md) | effective boundary constraint, of a composite: the relation its interconnected parts impose on the variables an outside system can reach, once the interior is eliminated; instantaneous or history-dependent, and possibly of a kind the parts' relations could not state | What [CLAIM-480](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md) demonstrates and [CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md), [QUESTION-283](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-283.md) and [CASE-179](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-179.md) use. A composite presents the systems that interact with its boundary with a relation among its accessible variables. Its examples are the series spring's k₁k₂/(k₁ + k₂), Baez and Fong's black box, a memory kernel, and Hansen and Ghrist's three-way v₁ = v₂ + v₃. The term fixes three points: the relation is a constraint whether instantaneous or history-dependent; it is effective, not a new fundamental law; and it can exceed the parts' relational vocabulary. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [TERM-091](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-091.md) | relational vocabulary, of a class of descriptions: the arities and kinds of relation it can state (pairwise or higher-order, among states or among histories, of which declared types), and so which constraints are expressible in it at all | What [QUESTION-283](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-283.md) asks about: whether composition can force a description to adopt relations its parts never needed. A luria record's relational vocabulary is its declared relation types and fields, and amendments that add one ([ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md), [ADR-044](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-044.md)) enlarge it. | [TERM-092](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-092.md) | inquiry frontier, of an agent at a budget: the questions it can formulate and pursue to a stated standard with the concepts, records, tools, time and computation it actually has, distinct from the questions its language can express and from those that have answers | The object of [CLAIM-475](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-475.md), from A17 §§2 and 7 of the exchange of 2026-10-27. A question is on an agent's frontier if some procedure available to it, within its budget and horizon, makes the question determinate enough to pursue. Formulating counts against the budget as well as answering. The frontier moves when resources grow and when reusable specifications make formulation cheaper, and it can change shape as well as size. The term separates askable from expressible and from answerable, which [CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md)'s last failure turns on. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [TERM-093](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-093.md) | correspondence structure, and how it is held: the maps that say which local states or descriptions of interacting systems count as agreeing, distinct from the physical coupling between them, and held as formed, discovered or adapted | The object [CLAIM-471](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-471.md), [QUESTION-282](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-282.md), [CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md) and [CASE-179](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-179.md) all turn on. It is a family of comparison maps from local descriptions into shared spaces, whose joint kernel (the global sections) is what "compatible" and "glued" mean. It is not the coupling that moves the states. How a correspondence structure is held is one of three ways: formed by physical interconnection, discovered by measurement, or adapted by an apparatus. A claim using "gluing" should say which. Proposed: the word has been used in four entries in one evening, and the owner's review turned on keeping its senses apart. | Proposed |
